items.excerpt: Let’s say you are new to data analytics and need a report or data analysis of a file, multiple files, or a query from a data warehouse. How do you start? What do you do? The common path is probably to ask ChatGPT or use the chatbox available, paste the exported CSV into Excel, and make some edits. items.title: OneLake: The unified foundation for data, context, governance, and AI
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Most organizations' data is scattered across dozens of applications, clouds and services. Now that agents need to work across the entire business, organizations need to bring that data together in one place: one copy, open to every engine and team, without moving or duplicating it. Unified data gives agents reach, but to act with confidence they also need context: what the data means, how it connects to the business, who should see it and whether it can be trusted. OneLake is the single place for customers to unify their data estate. Shortcuts , mirroring , catalog federation and IQ Share bring multi-cloud, on-premises sources and databases and data platforms together into a single view of the data estate. The OneLake catalog provides a trusted place for organizations to easily explore, govern and secure data in OneLake. items.title: Bringing trusted Fabric IQ context to wherever people and agents work
items.excerpt: If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric. Over the past year, AI has moved from answering questions to doing the work. As the 2026 Microsoft Work Trend Index shows, people are now handing entire tasks to agents and directing several at once. Those agents plan, decide, and act across systems, with less human review at every step. Fabric IQ helps turn your organization's business knowledge into an advantage for people and agents. As agents take on more responsibility, that knowledge matters more than which model they run on. Every organization can use the same frontier models. What sets yours apart is its context layer: the definitions, metrics, relationships, and rules that describe how your business actually works. When you connect that context with knowledge from across the organization, people and agents can uncover insights and take informed action that reflects how the business operates. The organizations seeing results treat business context as shared infrastructure, built once and reused by every agent. Today at Microsoft Ignite 202
